title: Error
description:
The single error envelope for every agent-router error response. One shape for all four endpoints, so a client writes one error handler.

Every error carries the caller's OBLIGATION as a machine-readable field rather than leaving it to be inferred from the status code. That is the whole point of this envelope: a client that retries a 409 catalog_version_stale forever, or aborts on a 503 catalog_unavailable that would have cleared in two seconds, is a client that read the number and not the contract.

NOT EVERY FAILURE IS AN ERROR ENVELOPE. `no_eligible_placement` is answered as an HTTP 200 PlaceResult with status: unavailable, deliberately - see README 'Error taxonomy'. It is not in this enum, and a client must not wait for a 4xx to discover that nothing is available.

This schema is an addition to the layout story 35.2 required. It exists so the error examples are mechanically validated like every other example, rather than being prose in a README that nothing checks.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Stable across versions: a code is never re-pointed at a different condition, only added or (with a major bump) removed. Full taxonomy with per-endpoint applicability in README 'Error taxonomy'.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to log and to show an operator. Never contains credentials, bearer tokens, or the contents of a heartbeat's runtime.endpoint.

obligation.description:
What the caller must do next.

retry - the same request may succeed unchanged; back off first, and honour retry_after_seconds when present. Both /v1/route and /v1/place are side-effect free and safe to retry.
re-plan - the request as framed cannot be served; the caller must go back a step (call /v1/route again, relax a constraint, or obtain human authorization) and issue a DIFFERENT request. Re-sending the identical request is a loop.
abort - the caller is wrong or unauthorized. Fail the attempt and surface it. Do not retry, and do not work around it - `metered_denied` in particular must never be worked around by resending with allow_metered: true, which would defeat invariant 4.

http_status.description: The HTTP status this envelope was served with. Duplicated into the body on purpose: these documents are also the committed fixtures, and a fixture that does not state its own status is not self-describing enough to test against.

endpoint.description: Optional. Which endpoint produced this error; useful in fixtures and logs.

details.description: Optional, code-specific context. Open-ended by design so a code can gain detail without a contract bump, but never a place to hide a second error code - the `code` field is the only machine-readable discriminator.

field.description: For invalid_request: the offending request field, in dotted path form.

requested.description: For unknown_profile / unknown_placement_policy: the value the caller sent.

known.description: For unknown_profile / unknown_placement_policy: the names that do exist in the loaded catalog, so a caller can report the mismatch without a second round trip.

expected_catalog_version.description: For catalog_version_stale: the digest the router is actually serving.

received_catalog_version.description: For catalog_version_stale: the digest the caller asserted.

node.description: For node_identity_mismatch: the node id the payload claimed. The identity the CREDENTIAL is bound to is deliberately not echoed back - telling an unauthenticated caller which node its token belongs to is a disclosure, and R9's threat model assumes edge credentials can be stolen.

withheld.description: For metered_denied with no non-metered alternative: the metered option that was withheld, in the same shape as ExecutionProfile.metered_denied.withheld.

retry_after_seconds.description: Optional. Present when obligation is `retry` and the router can say how long to wait; mirrors the Retry-After header. null or absent means the caller picks its own backoff.

catalog_version.description: Optional. The catalog digest the router is serving, when it has one loaded. Absent on catalog_unavailable, which is precisely the case where it has none.
